payload.feature:
LANDING PR #387: a model seat whose charter cannot be read refuses to start (#372).

This branch (fix-372-unreadable-charter) was delivered by run fix-bug-372-an-unreadable-charte-bfe8bac1 at a3a55cac, which a clean-enough review shipped (REVIEW-RESIDUAL-OK, low). Pull-request CI then failed only on test (macos-latest): a_seat_whose_charter_is_gone_is_journaled_as_a_failure_to_start compared the refused charter's path as created, while the engine names it resolved, and macOS's temporary directory sits behind /var -> /private/var. Commit 22f74035 (by hand, test-only) canonicalises the expected path's directory; it was reproduced on Linux with TMPDIR behind a symlink, failing before and passing after.

This run lands the new head under decision 0051 so the contribution gate can vouch for it. It is NOT a new implementation: if verify and review are clean, nothing is edited. If a finding returns the branch to implement, fix exactly that finding, prove it with a test bound by a compiling mutation, commit one signed-off commit ending "Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>", and never push. Do not run scripts/coverage-exact.sh; the controller runs it. The reviewers should judge the whole branch against main, with the prior run's low residual (the exec carve-out ruling) as known context.

Change location: `openspec/changes/{change}`. Archive operation: ["openspec","archive","{change}","--yes"].

# OpenSpec archive

Folding a change is the last task: run the archive operation named above,
which moves the change directory under `openspec/changes/archive/` and
folds its deltas into `openspec/specs/`. Folding also records which change
wrote which capability, so every capability the change touched carries a
`## Provenance` list.

After the archive operation, open each capability's
`openspec/specs/<capability>/spec.md` that the change touched and append
exactly one line under a `## Provenance` heading held at the end of the
file:

`- \`<archived-directory-name>\` — folded <YYYY-MM-DD>`

`<archived-directory-name>` is the directory the archive operation
created under `openspec/changes/archive/`; `<YYYY-MM-DD>` is the day it
was folded. Append only: never rewrite, reorder or remove an existing
provenance line, because standing truth accumulates and is not edited into
a different meaning. The line is a pointer, not a summary — it names the
change and nothing else, and the why stays in the change directory.

house.content:
This realm is a Rust workspace. Production code is Rust under `crates/`; the
Rust-only architecture is recorded by decision 0009. Semantic changes carry a
decision document with status `proposed` because only the operator accepts one.
Intake seats read `README.md` and decisions 0004 and 0005 before framing a
commission, along with the code and history it touches.

The frozen v1 contracts under `contracts/`, the production table at
`policy/phase-machine.json`, `policy/schemas/`, and `reference/` are read-only.
A contract change lands as a new version file beside the old one, never as an
edit. The evaluator corpus under `fixtures/` is also frozen and is never
regenerated, only versioned.

Tests are part of every change. Extend the suite that proves the code, run
`cargo test --workspace`, compile `bundles/self`, and leave formatting, clippy,
and the exact-coverage gate clean before reporting success.

Commit completed work with `git` using the repository's message style. Never
push.

## Release configuration

The release manager prepares the candidate and profile patches; the operator
publishes them. Local validation is preparation work. Remote CI on the final PR
head, publication, channel updates and live-profile verification are handoff
steps, recorded as pending until their remote results exist. Historical
"live from" channel versions and old journal examples are historical facts,
not current-version references to replace.

members.adversarial:
Adversarial review of the whole branch (a3a55cac + 22f74035) against main ba52724e. No new finding above low; the one residual is the prior run's already-ruled exec carve-out, kept visible as tracked debt. Verdict: shippable as tracked debt.

What I verified by trying to break it. (1) The production refusal is decision 0053's structural failure to start: run_seat_with computes effect_id/attempt_id then render_prompt BEFORE the result_path dir is created and BEFORE the secret store is opened, and on StartRefusal sends exactly one Result{Failed} with no accepted and no checkpoint. The engine's failed_to_start (Failed && !accepted && checkpoints empty && !deadline_killed) consumes that shape and journals start_failure, so a model seat whose charter is deleted after compile fails to start and the chain descends. (2) Ordering edge: if a seat has BOTH an unreadable charter and a missing secret, the charter refusal now wins and is fail-to-start where the secret-only path deliberately sends accepted; deliberate, and defensible (charter is more fundamental), not a defect. (3) render_prompt has exactly one production caller (run_seat_with); every other call site is tests. Model kinds (claude/lanetally/codex/dsh) always compile a canonical non-empty role via bundle.rs parse_role (dir canonicalized at bundle.rs:1057) or agents/load.rs; only exec compiles role_path empty, which is why the Exec arm is required. (4) The refusal does not create the result file or parent, and no checkpoint/accepted precedes it, so a refused attempt cannot be mistaken for mid-session work.

The test-only head (22f74035). The canonicalization is correct: compile canonicalizes the bundle dir, so an unreadable charter is named by its resolved path; tempdir returns the path as created, so on macOS's /var -> /private/var the concrete-file test needed parent-canonicalize + file_name. I reproduced the symlink condition on Linux by setting TMPDIR to a symlinked directory: a_seat_whose_charter_is_gone_is_journaled_as_a_failure_to_start passes with the fix (I could not revert the tracked test under the read-only rule, but I confirmed the engine canonicalizes at bundle.rs:1057, which is exactly the failing difference). It changes no production behavior.

Gates I ran: cargo fmt --all -- --check (exit 0); cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings (exit 0); git diff --check origin/main...HEAD (exit 0); git diff --stat over contracts/ policy/ phase-machine.json policy/schemas/ fixtures/ reference/ is empty (frozen surfaces untouched); cargo test -p brokkr-protocol --lib adapters (339 passed); -p brokkr-cli --test driver_conformance (25 passed) and --test agent_fallback (7 passed); -p brokkr-runtime full crate (488+ passed, 0 failed). Working tree clean at 22f74035.

Residual (low, known context, no hold): read_charter's arm `Err(_) if kind == AdapterKind::Exec => Ok(String::new())` means an exec-kind site that DECLARED `role` whose file becomes unreadable after compile runs with an empty charter. Concrete inputs -> output: bundle with an exec verify seat `role: roles/x.md` (parse_role accepts it at compile because the file exists) whose x.md is deleted before the run -> the exec script's prompt is missing its charter and the attempt does not refuse. Same fail-open shape as #372, narrow: no shipped bundle or recipe exec site declares a role (bundles/verify's verify seat is exec with no role; all `"role"` declarations I found are model seats), it is exec's pre-existing behavior, and the alternative (refuse a declared unreadable exec charter) breaks the boxed-gate case because the bundle holding the charter is not mounted in the namespace (delivered_by_brokkr::a_namespace_judged_run_carries_no_adjective). The prior review chief already asked the operator to rule between (a) exec charter optional, as implemented, and (b) refuse a declared unreadable exec charter by mounting it into the box. I agree with low and add no new weight. Not a security residual for shipped content.

Non-findings I deliberately dropped: a readable but EMPTY charter still runs a model seat (the issue scopes unreadable/missing only; many tests use /dev/null intentionally); MissingCorrelation is unreachable from production because the engine's process.rs always sends both ids (defensive, unit-covered); several runtime resume_tests still carry a relative role.md under fake drivers (test-only trap, harmless today).
members.correctness: Reviewed the whole branch fix-372-unreadable-charter against main (ba52724e): a3a55cac (typed StartRefusal; render_prompt -> Result; run_seat_with refuses a missing effect_id/attempt_id or an unreadable model charter before any spawn, before the secret store is opened, and before any accepted/checkpoint — verified in code order against decision 0053's failed_to_start shape) and 22f74035 (test-only: canonicalise the expected charter directory so macOS's /var -> /private/var TMPDIR matches the engine's resolved path — the premise checks out against agents/load.rs, which canonicalises the library root and the charter path, and the charter's parent still exists at assertion time since only the file is removed). Nothing was edited by this seat; HEAD is 22f74035 with a clean tree. Evidence: cargo test --workspace --all-features --locked fully green (the only failures on the first pass were three git-spawn lib tests tripping this box's broken GIT_CONFIG_COUNT env — they pass with GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0 set and passed on PR CI), the three new #372 tests pass individually, cargo fmt --all -- --check clean, cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -D warnings clean. render_prompt has exactly one production caller, so the signature change is contained; the conformance fixtures now carry a real charter, which correctly models the new invariant, and the shims' result-path extraction is unaffected by the prepended charter text. /dev/null as a readable empty charter in unit tests is valid on both CI OSes (matrix is ubuntu+macos only). Fit is good: not overbuilt, idiomatic thiserror, tests prove the refusal at three levels (adapter body, wire conformance over all four model drivers with no provider spawned, end-to-end journal start_failure). Residuals: (1, low, carried from the prior run's adjudicated ruling) the exec carve-out in read_charter — an exec site whose declared charter cannot be read still starts with an empty charter; documented in the doc comment and required by a_namespace_judged_run_carries_no_adjective, so accepted, not re-litigated. (2, info) the missing-correlation refusal emits a failed body with empty effect_id/attempt_id; production starts always name correlation (the protocol's Start requires both fields), so this branch is defensive and its journaling side is unproven end-to-end — behavior is no worse than the old empty-default path. (3, info) no decision document names the unreadable-charter refusal itself; it routes a new cause through decision 0053's already-ruled pre-session failure-to-start class and the prior review shipped the commit, so recorded as context only. No security smell.

result.notes:
Chief ruling: residual (low), matching the panel's floor. No security residual and no spec defect. Nothing was edited. HEAD is 22f74035 and the tree is clean.

Panel: the result was 'residual' with max severity low. Both members, correctness and adversarial, ruled residual. The brief names the second position 'security', but the member here is 'adversarial', which is this recipe's naming. It covered the security surface and found no security smell. Neither member's notes address the gate or argue for a lower result, so there is no injection finding.

My own read of origin/main...HEAD (9 files):
- render_prompt now returns Result<String, StartRefusal>. Its only production caller is run_seat_with. The refusal is checked before result_path's directory is created, before the secret store is opened and before any accepted or checkpoint, so it has decision 0053's failure-to-start shape.
- Every production start names both ids: process.rs Body::Start, used by the engine and by the oneshot path Muninn uses.
- Every model-kind site compiles a charter that parse_role or agents/load checked exists. Only exec and dialect sites compile role_path="", and they run as AdapterKind::Exec. So a legitimate seat is never refused.
- I re-ran the three #372 tests and all pass: the adapters unit test, conformance across claude/lanetally/codex/dsh, and the end-to-end journal start_failure test. I also ran the end-to-end test with TMPDIR behind a symlink, which reproduces macOS /var -> /private/var, and it passes. So the test-only head 22f74035 is sound.

Surviving findings, deduplicated:
1. [low; raised by correctness and adversarial] The exec carve-out in read_charter: `Err(_) if kind == AdapterKind::Exec => Ok(String::new())`. An exec site that declared a role whose file becomes unreadable after compile still starts, with an empty charter. No shipped bundle or recipe has such a site. The carve-out is required by a_namespace_judged_run_carries_no_adjective, because the boxed gate cannot see the bundle. The operator's ruling between (a) optional, as built, and (b) mount it and refuse is still owed. Not re-litigated here.
2. [info; correctness] The missing-correlation refusal (which now covers exec too) sends a failed body with empty ids. This is unreachable from production, it is unit-covered, and its journal side is unproven end-to-end.
3. [info; correctness] No decision document names the unreadable-charter refusal. It uses decision 0053's existing failure-to-start class.

Dropped as non-findings (adversarial): a readable but empty charter still runs; when a charter and a secret both fail, the charter refusal wins; test-only relative role.md fixtures under fake drivers.
